title: Prospective PhD Students
deadline: Ongoing / subject to program and funding availability
summary: Prospective doctoral students interested in precision medicine, pharmacogenomics, clinical informatics, real-world evidence, or healthcare AI may contact the lab to discuss research fit and current availability.
body_html:
Thomas Lab welcomes inquiries from prospective doctoral students whose interests align with the lab’s research program. Admission, funding, and start dates depend on the relevant graduate program and available support, so an inquiry is not a guarantee of an open funded position.

Strong candidates will be interested in rigorous clinical research questions and in developing reproducible computational or quantitative methods that can translate to patient care.
qualifications: Interest in pharmacogenomics, precision medicine, clinical NLP, real-world evidence, health outcomes, or trustworthy healthcare AI
Strong quantitative, computational, clinical, or pharmacy background appropriate to the proposed work
Ability to communicate clearly and work collaboratively across disciplines
Commitment to reproducible and responsible research
how_to_apply: Send a concise email describing your research interests and why they align with the lab
Attach a current CV or résumé
Include relevant academic background and research experience
When applicable, identify the UGA graduate program and intended admission cycle
funding: Subject to graduate-program and project funding availability; confirm before applying.
eligibility: Applicants must satisfy the requirements of the relevant University of Georgia graduate program.
International applicants should review program-specific English-language and immigration requirements.
Funding, admission, and supervision availability must be confirmed separately.

title: Research Assistants & Student Researchers
summary: Students interested in contributing to data-driven medication research can inquire about current research-assistant, independent-study, or project-based opportunities.
body_html:
Research needs vary over time. Depending on current projects, students may contribute to literature review, data curation, clinical NLP, reproducible analysis, software tooling, visualization, or manuscript preparation.

The most useful inquiry briefly explains the skills you can contribute, the skills you hope to develop, and the amount of time you can realistically commit.
qualifications: Interest in clinical or translational research
Reliable communication and attention to research quality
Relevant experience in data analysis, programming, pharmacy, clinical research, statistics, or scientific writing is helpful
Willingness to learn reproducible research workflows
how_to_apply: Email the lab with a short statement of interest
List relevant coursework, technical skills, and prior research experience
State your expected availability and timeframe
funding: Varies by project; some opportunities may be paid, for credit, or volunteer-based.
eligibility: Enrollment, work authorization, course-credit rules, and appointment eligibility depend on the specific opportunity.
The lab will state the arrangement clearly before any commitment is made.

title: Research Collaborations
summary: Clinicians, data scientists, pharmacists, informaticians, and research groups with complementary expertise can contact the lab about aligned collaborative questions.
body_html:
Collaborative inquiries are most useful when they begin with a well-defined clinical or translational question, a clear description of the available data or expertise, and a realistic view of the contribution expected from each team.

The lab is particularly interested in collaborations involving pharmacogenomics, cardiovascular pharmacotherapy, medication safety, clinical NLP, real-world evidence, and precision therapeutics.
qualifications: A clearly defined research question or complementary capability
Alignment with the lab’s scientific scope
Commitment to transparent, reproducible, and responsible research
how_to_apply: Describe the proposed roles and available data or resources
Include relevant timelines and expected outputs
funding: Project dependent; collaborative funding arrangements are discussed case by case.
eligibility: A collaboration should have a clear scientific question, complementary expertise or data, and an agreed scope of work.
